source.title: The relation of empathy to prosocial and related behaviors

confidence_rationale: Quantitative review directly on Q-091's methodological question: which MEASURE of empathy tracks genuine other-directed behaviour. It finds physiological and facial/expressive measures correlate with prosocial behaviour more strongly than self-report/verbal measures, and -- the load-bearing point -- physiological indices are LESS subject to voluntary, top-down manipulation than verbal or facial responses. That is exactly the property Q-091's evaluation needs: a channel an agent cannot fake by choosing what to say. Source quality high (Psychological Bulletin meta-analytic review, heavily cited). Held at 0.68 because it concerns measurement of empathy in humans, not the masking of absent empathy by a fluent LANGUAGE system specifically, and it predates and does not address artificial agents.
failure_signatures: Self-reported / verbal empathy measures correlate more weakly with actual prosocial behaviour than physiological and facial measures do -- so a verbal channel is the WEAKEST evidentiary basis for inferring genuine other-directed disposition.

Verbal and facial responses are subject to voluntary top-down manipulation in a way physiological responses are not -- an agent can produce the report it judges will be well-received, which is precisely the capacity a fluent language system has in abundance.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Across studies, empathy relates positively to prosocial behaviour, but the strength of the relation depends heavily on how empathy is measured: physiological and facial/expressive indices correlate with prosocial behaviour more strongly than self-report (including verbal) measures, and physiological assessments are less subject to voluntary, top-down manipulation by the subject than facial or verbal responses.
mapping.ree_translation: This gives Q-091's answer its measurement-theoretic spine: the more a channel is under the subject's voluntary control, the worse it is as evidence of genuine other-directed disposition -- and a linguistic channel is maximally voluntary. It supports designing REE's empathy evaluation around a signal the agent cannot strategically produce (a costly other-directed action under live alternatives; residue after exploiting a cooperating other, per MECH-407), analogous to the human physiological index, rather than around the language channel that is the machine equivalent of the manipulable verbal self-report.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The human 'physiological measure' has no literal REE analogue -- REE has no autonomic system -- so the transfer is by ANALOGY of the underlying property (involuntary, hard-to-fake) rather than of the measure itself. The paper also concerns how well a measure tracks empathy that IS present, not how a fluent system masks empathy that is ABSENT; the inference to the masking case is one step of reasoning beyond what it directly shows. It is a human developmental/social-psychology finding, pre-dating artificial agents entirely.
mapping.source_context: Meta-analytic review of the human empathy-prosociality literature (developmental and social psychology); compares empathy operationalisations (self-report, facial/expressive, physiological) against prosocial-behaviour outcomes.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (Psychological Bulletin meta-analysis). Mapping fidelity moderate-good: it directly addresses the measurement question (which channel is trustworthy) that Q-091's answer turns on, but by analogy of the manipulability property rather than a like-for-like measure, and for present-empathy rather than absent-empathy masking. Transfer risk 0.5: no autonomic analogue in REE, 1987 human data to a V4 artificial substrate.
